nodes.label: Arena OS Redesign Vision (Challenge Operating System)
nodes.rationale: Reframes Arena from 'a place with challenges' (18 labels on one generic code-editor environment, library-first homepage) into one shell + one assignment engine + one proof pipeline + eighteen real work environments; inverts the 'label-over-environment' root disease behind system-design-in-a-markdown-box and dashboards that only appear after submission.

nodes.label: Contract A: Environment Fidelity
nodes.rationale: A challenge may only ship if its workstation contains the tools the real role actually uses; if the right workstation doesn't exist yet, the challenge waits — this is the quality gate that permanently kills 'generic editor with a different label'.

nodes.label: Contract B: Live Truth
nodes.rationale: Run/Validate/Preview all operate on the live workspace with real execution (WASM SQL/Python, sandboxed iframes, deterministic simulators) before submission; the user must never submit blind just to see their own output.

nodes.label: Contract C: Frozen Proof
nodes.rationale: Submit is the only destructive-ish action: it freezes the attempt into an immutable submission, scores it, and mints a recruiter-visible ProofDoc; the Submissions tab is an archive of frozen attempts, never the birthplace of output.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Architecture (L1-L4)
nodes.rationale: L1 Arena Core (assignment engine, ELO economy, execution engines) -> L2 Universal Challenge Shell -> L3 sixteen lazy-loaded Workstation Renderers -> L4 Proof Pipeline; a new domain is added by writing one L3 module, L1/L2/L4 never fork.

nodes.label: Challenge Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: ASSIGNED -> OPENED -> IN_PROGRESS (autosave) <-> VALIDATED(n) -> SUBMITTED (frozen) -> SCORED -> PROOFED; one single state machine runs identically for every domain and every workstation.

nodes.label: Assignment Engine (Mission Queue)
nodes.rationale: One ordered Mission Queue per user fed by four generators (Daily Mission, Adaptive Repair, Recruiter Challenges, Self-queued), ordered recruiter(deadline asc) -> daily -> repair -> self-queued; the homepage renders the queue, not a library.

nodes.label: One ELO Economy
nodes.rationale: Global ELO = weighted blend of role ELOs (active role x1.0, others x0.3); validation never changes ELO, only SCORED submissions do — keeps validating psychologically safe as 'how you work', not 'how you're judged'.

nodes.label: Mission Desk Homepage Redesign
nodes.rationale: Reorders the homepage around 'reporting for duty': Readiness Strip -> Mission Hero/Queue -> Proof Shelf -> only then the Practice Library below the fold; target time-to-mission-start < 10s.

nodes.label: Universal Challenge Shell
nodes.rationale: Identical outer frame for all 18 domains: top bar, left prompt rail (Brief/Data/Hints/History), center workstation renderer slot, right context rail (Live Checklist/Proof Preview), and a persistent 4-slot action bar (Run/Validate/Preview/Submit).

nodes.label: 16 Workstation Families (W1-W18)
nodes.rationale: Code IDE, Frontend Sandbox, API Workstation, Fullstack Studio, SQL Lab, Notebook Lab, BI Dashboard Studio, Data Pipeline Studio, Infra Terminal, Cloud Architecture Lab, SRE Console, Security Console, SOC IR Console, QA Test Lab, Analysis Board, Mobile Studio, AI/LLM Studio, System Design Workspace — each a self-contained renderer module with its own execution model (client-wasm/client-sandbox/simulated/server).

nodes.label: 18-Domain Routing Table (§6)
nodes.rationale: Every role maps to a primary workstation plus secondaries chosen by asking 'what does this person's screen look like at work,' making the two historic offenders (system design in markdown, analyst output hidden until submission) structurally impossible via a workspace-allowlist validated at authoring time.

nodes.label: Four-Slot Action Contract (§7)
nodes.rationale: Primary Run / Validate / Preview Proof / Submit are fixed bottom-bar slots with per-workstation labels; 'Run Tests' exists only where it's the actual job (W14) or the universal judge harness (W1) — canvas/document workstations hide the Run slot rather than inventing a fake verb.

nodes.label: Validation vs Submission Logic (§8)
nodes.rationale: Validation is formative (unlimited, free, deterministic-only, mutates the live workspace, never touches ELO); submission is summative (scarce, immutable, adds AI evaluation, applies ELO). The old product blurred these — Validate buttons that did nothing and output only materializing at submission.

nodes.label: W7 BI Dashboard Studio
nodes.rationale: Data -> Build -> Present three-tab loop mirroring the analyst's real day; publishing a query result as KPI/Trend/Breakdown is the explicit bridge from computation to presentation, and Validate Metrics visibly mutates the Present dashboard (red outline on failing cards) rather than hiding output until submission.

nodes.label: W18 System Design Workspace
nodes.rationale: An architecture canvas is the workspace, not a markdown editor; Check Completeness runs the rubric as executable rules (orphan-node detection, required layers per prompt class, capacity arithmetic tolerance) that annotate the canvas directly.

nodes.label: ProofDoc Model (§16)
nodes.rationale: Every scored submission mints one portable, recruiter-renderable ProofDoc: artifact-first (thumbnail is the dashboard/diagram/report, not a number), honest metadata (hints/attempt-number/validation-count disclosed), and replayable (dataset_seed + frozen inputs allow deterministic re-execution for anti-cheat/recruiter confidence).

nodes.label: WorkstationModule Contract (§19.2)
nodes.rationale: A TypeScript interface (init/restore/collectValidatables/applyValidation/buildProofDraft/freeze/renderFrozen) that every workstation module must implement to register at all — Contracts B and C are enforced by the type system, not by review discipline.

nodes.label: Challenge JSON Authoring Schema (§19.4)
nodes.rationale: Versioned authoring format binding role, workstation, stack_variants, validation checks, and proof_recipe; authoring CI rejects workstation/role mismatches, checks whose locus isn't in the declared panels, and any challenge with zero deterministic checks.

nodes.label: Supabase Data Model (§19.5)
nodes.rationale: attempts and scores tables carry no UPDATE policy at all in RLS — frozen means frozen at the database layer, not just an app-level convention.

nodes.label: 4-Phase Build Order (§20.1)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 ships the spine on the three workstations that already have real engines (W7/W5/W6, sql.js+Pyodide) to prove the whole thesis on the analyst cluster first; Phase 2 engineering, Phase 3 ops/simulation kit (shared vmModel+scenarioPlayer), Phase 4 long tail.

nodes.label: Five Hardest Risks & Mitigations (§20.2)
nodes.rationale: Simulator credibility (fewer, deeper scenarios > many shallow), Pyodide weight on Indian bandwidth (service-worker cache + lite-validation path), AI-scoring trust (deterministic floor >=60% of rubric), content velocity (challenge JSON + seed factory make variants cheap), and cheating/proof integrity (seeded per-user datasets + server re-execution + env_hash replay).
